architecture.drive: DIRECT DRIVE — gearbox deleted in favour of a tuned Kv
architecture.esc: drone-arm Rev-B, 6 channels, 12S, sensorless FOC, <=60 A/channel

poleCountAnswer.question: is 2 pole pairs terrible for efficiency?
poleCountAnswer.answer: No — at high mechanical speed fewer pole pairs gives LOWER electrical frequency, so LOWER iron (hysteresis+eddy) loss. A 2-pole-pair motor at 41,070 rpm runs at ~1,369 Hz, essentially the same frequency as a 7-pole-pair motor at 12,500 rpm (~1,458 Hz), so the direct-drive rewind is not penalised. Fewer poles does reduce torque-per-amp (more copper loss for a given torque) and motor inductance, but at this high speed iron loss dominates, so low pole count is the right choice. Pole count is set by the rotor magnets and is NOT changed by a rewind.

gearboxVsDirect.conclusion: Deleting the gearbox removes the 5% gear loss and the 0.72 kg gearbox, and keeps the same electrical frequency, so direct drive wins. It requires a rewound Kv of ~925 (80 mm) and a rotor/bearing/containment rating for ~41 krpm.

rewindMachine.approach: attachment for the existing TwoTrees 3018 Pro CNC — replace the spindle tool with a 3D-printed winding mandrel; the CNC X/Z axes do the wire traverse and the spindle rotates the mandrel

items.item: 3D printed winding mandrel + stator holder + wire guide + tensioner (PLA/PETG)
Hall-effect sensor + magnet ring for turn counting (or optical flag)
Wiring, connectors, mandrel insert, fasteners, misc

rewindMachine.note: one-time tool; reuses the CNC so no gantry/stepper/driver/controller spend; per-motor wire/consumables shown separately

cost.note: if the winder is a reusable tool it is not charged to the six-motor ceiling; if it is, the build exceeds INR 24000 by INR 54
